summary.intent: Fix desktop E2E test failures related to FilePointer publish timing and inode errors, then verify CI passes for both web and desktop.
summary.outcome: The inode error was fixed (PR #448), and the FilePointer publish timeout was doubled from 60s to 120s (12→24 attempts) in both shell and PowerShell test scripts. A fresh CI run was triggered.

repo: Desktop E2E round-trip tests use polling loops of 12 attempts × 5s = 60s for FilePointer publish; this is insufficient in CI due to debounce + IPFS upload + IPNS publish chain taking just over 60s.
Web E2E has a known flaky test: batch-download upload test fails intermittently due to Sapphire Devnet epoch rotation (wallet login timeout), not code issues.
Test 4 (fresh client reload) passes after test 3 (FilePointer timeout) fails, confirming the data IS published — the issue is purely timing/polling window.

code.finding: Polling loop bumped from 12 to 24 attempts (60s → 120s window) to accommodate slow IPFS/IPNS publish in CI.
Both the FilePointer publish polling loop and the IPNS resolve polling loop bumped from 12 to 24 attempts.

workflow: Checking whether a later test step passes is a useful signal to distinguish timeout flakiness from true failures.
CI E2E run was triggered by pushing the commit directly; results checked via Bash CI status commands.

friction: The 60s FilePointer timeout has been too tight in CI since at least April 2 (PR #446), meaning this was a pre-existing latent issue that took multiple PRs to surface clearly.
Web E2E has a recurring Sapphire Devnet epoch flakiness that produces false-alarm failures and requires manual triage each CI run.
open_items: Verify that doubling the timeout (24 attempts × 5s) is sufficient in CI, or consider reducing the publish debounce delay as an alternative fix.
Investigate and potentially suppress or fix the Sapphire Devnet epoch flakiness in the batch-download web E2E test.
The root cause of slow IPFS/IPNS publish in CI (debounce + upload + IPNS chain > 60s) may warrant a deeper performance investigation.
